newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Stadshypotek has no plan to meet minister.
newsitem.headline: Stadshypotek has no plan to meet minister.

text.p: The head of Stadshypotek's board on Thursday said he had no plans to meet Sweden's finance minister, who this week expressed no confidence in the board over a plan to merge with insurance company Skandia.
"We have no plans for that now," Stadshypotek board chairman Gosta Renell told Reuters.

Finance Minister Erik Asbrink, who is supervising the sale of the state's 34 percent shareholding in Stadshypotek, slammed a proposal by Stadshypotek, Sweden's largest mortgage bank, to merge with Skandia to form what it called the Nordic region's leading financial institution with total assets of 500 billion crowns.

Asbrink said on Monday he had no confidence in the board of Stadshypotek, which has about one third of the Swedish market, accusing them of failing to consult the state shareholder about the merger plan.
In an open letter to Asbrink, the board members said they had no intention of resigning and that the merger would benefit all its shareholders.
The government plans to sell its 34 percent stake through a controlled auction to industrial buyers.
